name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_505
nl_statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $a\in R$. Show that $a\cdot 0 = 0 = 0\cdot a$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_507
nl_statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $a,b\in R$. Show that $a(-b) = -(ab) = (-a)b$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_509
nl_statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $a,b\in R$. Show that $(-a)(-b) = ab$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_511
nl_statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $a,b,c\in R$. Show that $a(b-c) = ab - ac$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_513
nl_statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $a\in R$. Show that $(-1)a = -a$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_607
nl_statement: Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer and let $a,b,c\in \mathbb{Z}$. Show that if $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ and $b \equiv c \pmod{n}$, then $a \equiv c \pmod{n}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_671
nl_statement: Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer and let $a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{Z}$. Suppose that $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ and $c \equiv d \pmod{n}$. Show that $a+c \equiv b+d \pmod{n}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_779
nl_statement: Let $n>0$ be an integer and let $a,b \in \mathbb{Z}$. Prove that $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ if and only if $a$ and $b$ have the same remainder upon division by $n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_782
nl_statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $a,b,c \in R$. Prove each of the following: $a \cdot 0 = 0 = 0 \cdot a$, $a(-b) = -(ab) = (-a)b$, $(-a)(-b) = ab$, $a(b-c) = ab - ac$, and $(-1)a = -a$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_815
nl_statement: Define a relation $\approx$ on $\mathbb{R}$ by $a \approx b$ if and only if $a-b \in \mathbb{Z}$. Prove that $\approx$ is an equivalence relation on $\mathbb{R}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_828
nl_statement: Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer and let $a,b,c,d\in \mathbb{Z}$ with $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ and $c \equiv d \pmod{n}$. Prove that $a+c \equiv b+d \pmod{n}$ and $ac \equiv bd \pmod{n}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_901
nl_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. A congruence class $[a] \in \mathbb{Z}_n$ is a unit if and only if $\gcd(a,n) = 1$. Hence, the set $\mathbb{Z}_n^{\times}$ of units in $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is equal to $\{ [a] \in \mathbb{Z}_n : \gcd(a,n) = 1 \}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_930
nl_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Then $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is a field if and only if $n$ is a prime number.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_970
nl_statement: Prove that a commutative ring $R$ is a field if and only if $R^{\times} = R\setminus\{0\}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_1021
nl_statement: Let $n>1$ be an integer. Prove that the linear congruence $ax \equiv b \pmod{n}$ has a solution in $\mathbb{Z}_n$ whenever the class $[a] \in \mathbb{Z}_n$ is a unit.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Sylow_625
nl_statement: Two permutations in $S_n$ are conjugate if and only if they have the same cycle type. Hence, the partitions of $n$ label the conjugacy classes of $S_n$. The number of distinct conjugacy classes equals the number of partitions of $n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Sylow_394
nl_statement: Let $p$ be a prime. Prove that if $G$ is a finite group with exactly one Sylow $p$-subgroup, then that Sylow $p$-subgroup is normal in $G$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Sylow_402
nl_statement: Prove that if $G$ is a finite group in which every element has order a power of a fixed prime $p$, then $\lvert G\rvert = p^r$ for some integer $r\ge 1$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Sylow_421
nl_statement: Show that if $\lvert G\rvert = 2p$ where $p$ is an odd prime, then $G$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}_{2p}$ or $D_{p}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Sylow_771
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 6$ and let $N$ be a proper normal subgroup of $A_n$. For a fixed $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $G_i=\{\sigma\in A_n:\sigma(i)=i\}$ be the subgroup of permutations that fix $i$. Show that $N$ contains $G_i$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Sylow_777
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 6$ and let $N$ be a proper normal subgroup of $A_n$. Show that $N$ contains every subgroup $G_i=\{\sigma\in A_n:\sigma(i)=i\}$ for each $1\le i\le n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abelian_290
nl_statement: Any finite abelian group is isomorphic to a direct product of cyclic groups. If $n=p_{1}^{k_{1}}\cdots p_{r}^{k_{r}}$ is the prime power factorization of $n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of finite abelian groups of order $n$ is $p(k_{1})\cdots p(k_{r})$, where $p(k)$ denotes the number of partitions of $k$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abelian_389
nl_statement: Prove that for integers $m,n\ge 1$ with $\gcd(m,n)=1$, one has $\mathbb{Z}_{m}\times \mathbb{Z}_{n}\cong \mathbb{Z}_{mn}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abelian_396
nl_statement: Let $p$ be a prime. Show that the composition factors of any finite abelian $p$-group are all isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_{p}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_618
nl_statement: Let $G=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} a & -b\\ b & a \end{bmatrix}: a,b\in\mathbb{R}\right\}$. Prove that $G$ is a group under matrix addition and construct an isomorphism $(\mathbb{C},+)\cong G$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_649
nl_statement: Let $R$ be a set with two binary operations $+$ and $\cdot$. Show that $R$ is a ring if and only if: (1) $(R,+)$ is an abelian group with identity $0$; (2) $(R,\cdot)$ is a monoid with identity $1$; and (3) $a(b+c)=ab+ac$ and $(b+c)a=ba+ca$ for all $a,b,c\in R$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_665
nl_statement: Let $F$ be a set with two binary operations $+$ and $\cdot$. Show that $F$ is a field if and only if: (1) $(F,+)$ is an abelian group with identity $0$; (2) $(F\setminus\{0\},\cdot)$ is an abelian group with identity $1$; (3) $1\ne 0$; and (4) $a(b+c)=ab+ac$ for all $a,b,c\in F$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_932
nl_statement: Prove that the subgroups of $(\mathbb{Z},+)$ are exactly the subgroups $n\mathbb{Z}$ for integers $n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_942
nl_statement: Let $F$ be a field, let $G$ be a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, and define $H=\{A\in G:\det A=\pm 1\}$. Prove that $H$ is a subgroup of $G$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_1075
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 3$. Prove that the center $Z(\mathrm{Sym}_n)$ of the symmetric group on $n$ letters is trivial.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_1109
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 2$. Prove that $\mathrm{Sym}_n$ is generated by the set $S=\{(1,2),(1,2,3,\dots,n)\}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_actions_705
nl_statement: Let $G$ be a group of order $p^r$ where $p$ is prime and $r\ge 1$. Prove that $|Z(G)|=p^k$ for some integer $k\ge 1$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_cyclic-gps_158
nl_statement: Any infinite cyclic group is isomorphic to the additive group $\mathbb{Z}$ of integers. Any finite cyclic group is isomorphic to the additive group $\mathbb{Z}_n$ of integers modulo $n$, for some positive integer $n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_cyclic-gps_271
nl_statement: There is a primitive root in the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}_n^{\times}$ if and only if $n=2$, $4$, $p^t$, or $2p^t$, where $p$ is an odd prime.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_cosets_492
nl_statement: Let $H$ and $K$ be finite subgroups of a group $G$ with $|H|=m$ and $|K|=n$. Prove that if $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then $H\cap K=\{1\}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_204
nl_statement: For any positive integer $n$, if $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix and $B$ is the matrix obtained from $A$ by performing a single elementary row operation, then $B=UA$, where $U$ is the corresponding elementary $n\times n$ elementary matrix of the same type.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_215
nl_statement: Any nonsingular $n\times n$ real matrix $A$ can be expressed as a product of elementary matrices.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_348
nl_statement: Show that $\mathrm{GL}(n)=\{A\in \operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathbb{R}):\det A\neq 0\}$ is a group under matrix multiplication.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_349
nl_statement: Show that $\mathrm{SL}(n)=\{A\in \operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathbb{R}):\det A=1\}$ is a group under matrix multiplication.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_352
nl_statement: Let $G\subseteq \operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ be a nonempty set closed under products and inverses (i.e., a matrix group). Prove that the identity matrix $I$ belongs to $G$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_358
nl_statement: Using $(AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}$ and $(AB)^{\mathsf{T}}=B^{\mathsf{T}}A^{\mathsf{T}}$, prove that $\mathrm{O}(n)=\{A\in \operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathbb{R}) : A A^{\mathsf{T}}=I\}$ is a group under matrix multiplication.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_366
nl_statement: Prove that $\mathrm{O}(n)=\{A\in \mathrm{GL}(n): A A^{\mathsf{T}}=I\}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_380
nl_statement: Let $A\in \mathrm{O}(n)$ with columns $A_1,\dots,A_n$. Deduce that $\{A_1,\dots,A_n\}$ is an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_385
nl_statement: Prove that $\mathrm{SO}(n)=\{A\in \mathrm{O}(n):\det A=1\}$ is a matrix group.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_392
nl_statement: Let $G,H\subset \mathrm{GL}(n)$ be matrix groups (each consisting of $n\times n$ matrices). Prove that $G\cap H$ is a matrix group.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_404
nl_statement: Let $D(n)$ be the set of all diagonal matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(n)$. Show that $D(n)$ is a matrix group.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_409
nl_statement: For $1\le i\ne j\le n$ and $t\in \mathbb{R}$, let $E_{ij}(t)$ denote the elementary matrix obtained from the identity by adding $t$ times row $j$ to row $i$. Prove that $E_{ij}(t)\in \mathrm{SL}(n)$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_411
nl_statement: Let $D_1(n)$ be the set of all diagonal matrices in $\mathrm{SL}(n)$. Show that $D_1(n)$ is a matrix group.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_484
nl_statement: The group $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ of all proper orthogonal $2\times 2$ matrices is exactly the set of rotation matrices $R_\theta=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix}, \quad \theta\in\mathbb{R}.$
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_552
nl_statement: The matrix group $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ is isomorphic to the group $\{\rho_\theta:\theta\in\mathbb{R}\}$ of rotations of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_577
nl_statement: For any $2\times 2$ improper orthogonal matrix $H$ (i.e., $H\in \mathrm{O}(2)$ and $\det H=-1$), the products $H_0H$ and $HH_0$ both belong to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, where $H_0=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{bmatrix}$ is reflection across the $x$-axis.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_582
nl_statement: For each $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$, the reflection of $\mathbb{R}^2$ across the line through the origin making angle $\theta$ with the $x$-axis is a linear operator, and its matrix $H_\theta$ is an improper orthogonal matrix (i.e., $H_\theta\in \mathrm{O}(2)$ and $\det H_\theta=-1$).
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_713
nl_statement: Show that the product of any two reflection matrices in $\mathrm{O}(2)$ is a rotation matrix (i.e., an element of $\mathrm{SO}(2)$).
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_836
nl_statement: Let $F$ be a field and $E(t)=\begin{bmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$ for $t\in F$. Show that $E(s)E(t)=E(s+t)$ for all $s,t\in F$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_838
nl_statement: Let $F$ be a field and $E(t)=\begin{bmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$ for $t\in F$. Show that $E(t)^{-1}=E(-t)$ for all $t\in F$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_839
nl_statement: Let $F$ be a field and $G=\{E(t): t\in F\}$ with $E(t)=\begin{bmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$. Prove that $G$ is a matrix group under multiplication.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_844
nl_statement: Let $F$ be a field and let $G$ be the set of all block matrices of the form $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\0&C\end{bmatrix}$ with $A,B,C\in \operatorname{Mat}_{2\times 2}(F)$ such that $\det(AC)\ne 0$. Verify that $G$ is a matrix group under multiplication.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_present_315
nl_statement: Show that the group given by the presentation $\langle a, b \mid a^5 = b^2 = 1,\; ba = a^2 b \rangle$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_present_327
nl_statement: Show that the quaternion group $Q=\{\pm 1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$, in which $i^2=j^2=k^2=-1$, $(-1)^2=1$, and the symbols $i,j,k$ multiply like standard unit vectors according to the usual cross-product rules in $\mathbb{R}^3$, is presented by $\langle a, b \mid a^2 = b^2 = (ab)^2 \rangle.$
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_perm-gps_805
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 1$ and let $S_n$ be the symmetric group on $\{1,\dots,n\}$. Show that every factorization of the identity permutation $id$ as a product of transpositions uses an even number of transpositions.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_perm-gps_867
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 1$ and let $S_n$ be the symmetric group on $\{1,\dots,n\}$. For any $\alpha,\beta\in S_n$, prove that $\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha\beta)=\operatorname{sgn}(\alpha)\operatorname{sgn}(\beta)$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_perm-gps_758
nl_statement: Let $\alpha=(1,2)$ and $\beta=(1,2,3)$ in $S_3$, and let $G=\langle \alpha,\beta\rangle$. Show that $G=S_3$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_perm-gps_777
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 2$. Prove that $S_n$ is generated by the set of adjacent transpositions $\{(1,2),(2,3),\dots,(n-1,n)\}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_perm-gps_789
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 2$. Prove that $S_n$ is generated by the two elements $S=\{(1,2),\,(1,2,3,\dots,n)\}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_products_322
nl_statement: Show that if $m,n$ are relatively prime then $C_{mn} \cong C_m \times C_n$. (Here, $C_n$ means the cyclic group of order $n$.)
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_products_363
nl_statement: Show that if $G = H_1 \times H_2 \times \cdots \times H_n$ is the internal direct product of normal subgroups $H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n$ then for any $i \ne j$ we have: $H_i \cap H_j = \{1\}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_products_372
nl_statement: Show that the map $\varphi:G \to G \times H$ given by $\varphi(x) = (x,1)$ is an injective homomorphism.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_simple-gps_257
nl_statement: Let $p(x)$ be an irreducible polynomial with rational coefficients, and let $G = \mathrm{Gal}(p)$ be its Galois group. Then the complex roots of $p(x)$ are expressible in terms of radicals if and only if $G$ is a solvable group.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_simple-gps_298
nl_statement: Assuming that $A_5$ is a simple group (this was proved by Galois) show that $S_5$ is not a solvable group.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_simple-gps_308
nl_statement: Galois proved that the alternating group $A_5$ is simple. Galois also showed that the symmetry group of the general quintic equation (degree 5 polynomial with arbitrary variable coefficients) is $S_5$. Assuming these facts, prove that the roots of a general quintic cannot be expressed in terms of radicals.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_simple-gps_359
nl_statement: Every finite simple group is isomorphic to one of the following groups: (1) A cyclic group of prime order. (2) An alternating group of degree at least 5. (3) A simple group of Lie type, including both (4) the classical Lie groups, namely the simple groups related to the projective special linear, unitary, symplectic, or orthogonal transformations over a finite field; (5) the exceptional and twisted groups of Lie type (including the Tits group). (6) One of the 26 sporadic simple groups.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_quotient-gps_300
nl_statement: Show that if $H$ is a subgroup of order $n$ in a group $G$ and $H$ is the only subgroup of order $n$, then $H \triangleleft\, G$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_quotient-gps_337
nl_statement: Show that $\mathrm{SL}(n) \triangleleft\, \mathrm{GL}(n)$ and that $\mathrm{GL}(n)/\mathrm{SL}(n)$ is isomorphic to the multiplicative group $\mathbb{R}^{\times}$ of the field of real numbers.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_quotient-gps_675
nl_statement: (Injectivity test for homomorphisms) Prove that if $f: G \to H$ is a group homomorphism with kernel $K$ then $f$ is injective if and only if $K$ is the trivial subgroup.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_quotient-gps_720
nl_statement: Prove that $\mathrm{SL}(n) \triangleleft\, \mathrm{GL}(n)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(n)/\mathrm{SL}(n) \cong \mathbb{R}^{\times}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_quotient-gps_723
nl_statement: Prove that $\mathrm{SO}(n) \triangleleft\, \mathrm{O}(n)$ and $\mathrm{O}(n)/\mathrm{SO}(n) \cong \mathbb{Z}^{\times}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_quotient-gps_730
nl_statement: If $H \triangleleft\, G$, $K \triangleleft\, G$, and $H \subset K$ then $(K/H) \triangleleft\, (G/H)$ and $(G/H)/(K/H) \cong G/K$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_symmetry_743
nl_statement: Let \(D_n\) be the dihedral group of a regular \(n\)-gon (\(n\ge 3\)). Let \(r\) be the rotation by \(2\pi/n\) and let \(h\) be the reflection across the horizontal axis. Prove that \(rhr=h\) by giving an algebraic argument with matrices (represent \(r\) by a rotation matrix and \(h\) by a suitable reflection matrix).
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_symmetry_760
nl_statement: Let \(F\) be a field. A permutation matrix in \(\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\) is an \(n\times n\) matrix obtained from the identity matrix by a permutation of its columns (equivalently, it has exactly one entry \(1\) in each row and each column, and all other entries are \(0\)). Prove that the symmetric group \(S_n\) is isomorphic to the subgroup of permutation matrices in \(\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\) via the map \(\alpha \mapsto P_\alpha\), where \(P_\alpha\) is the permutation matrix obtained by applying \(\alpha\in S_n\) to the columns of the identity matrix.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_symmetry_766
nl_statement: Let \(G\) be a group, \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), and \(F\) a field. Show that any permutation representation \(\delta: G \to S_n\) gives rise to a matrix representation \(\rho: G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\) by sending \(g\in G\) to the permutation matrix \(P_{\delta(g)}\).
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_500
nl_statement: Let $\rho_\theta:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be defined by $\rho_\theta(X)=R_\theta X$, where $R_\theta=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$. Show that $\rho_\theta$ is a rotation of $\mathbb{R}^2$ through $\theta$ radians; i.e., for any vector $X\in\mathbb{R}^2$, the vector $\rho_\theta(X)$ is obtained by rotating $X$ by angle $\theta$ about the origin.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_quotient-gps_341
nl_statement: Show that the set $G$ of all real $2 \times 2$ matrices of the form $\left( \begin{matrix} a&b\\ 0&c \end{matrix} \right)$ is a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}(2)$. Let $N$ be the set of all matrices of the form $\left( \begin{matrix} 1&b\\ 0&1 \end{matrix} \right).$ Prove that $N \triangleleft\, G$. (Note that you need to show it is a subgroup as well as prove that it is normal.)
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_1008
nl_statement: Let $\mathrm{O}(2)$ be the group of real $2\times 2$ orthogonal matrices and $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ the subgroup of rotations. Prove that $\mathrm{O}(2)$ is generated by $\mathrm{SO}(2)\cup\{A\}$ for any fixed improper orthogonal matrix $A\in \mathrm{O}(2)\setminus \mathrm{SO}(2)$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_629
nl_statement: $\mathrm{O}(2)=\{R_\theta:\theta\in\mathbb{R}\}\,\cup\,\{H_\theta:\theta\in\mathbb{R}\}$, where $R_\theta=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$ and $H_\theta$ is reflection across the line through the origin making angle $\theta$ with the $x$-axis.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_619
nl_statement: Let $G=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} a & -b\\ b & a \end{bmatrix}: a,b\in\mathbb{R}\right\}$ and let $G'=G\setminus\left\{\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}\right\}$. Prove that $G'$ is a group under matrix multiplication.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_719
nl_statement: Show that $R_{2\theta} H_0 R_{2\theta}=H_0$ for all $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$, where $H_0=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $R_{2\theta}=\begin{bmatrix}\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\ \sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)\end{bmatrix}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_705
nl_statement: Give a conceptual derivation (i.e., a proof) of the addition formulas for sine and cosine: $\cos(\theta_1+\theta_2)=\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2-\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2,\qquad \sin(\theta_1+\theta_2)=\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2+\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2,$ for all $\theta_1,\theta_2\in\mathbb{R}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_373
nl_statement: Let $A\in \mathrm{O}(n)$ with column vectors $A_1,\dots,A_n\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Show that $A_i^{\mathsf{T}}A_j=\delta_{ij}$ for all $1\le i,j\le n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_376
nl_statement: Let $A\in \mathrm{O}(n)$ with column vectors $A_1,\dots,A_n\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Show that $A_i\cdot A_j=\delta_{ij}$ for all $1\le i,j\le n$, where $\cdot$ denotes the standard dot product on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_529
nl_statement: For all $\theta,\theta_1,\theta_2\in\mathbb{R}$, we have $\rho_{\theta_1}\rho_{\theta_2}=\rho_{\theta_1+\theta_2}$ and $(\rho_\theta)^{-1}=\rho_{-\theta}$. In particular, rotations commute: $\rho_{\theta_1}\rho_{\theta_2}=\rho_{\theta_2}\rho_{\theta_1}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_725
nl_statement: Fix an integer $n>1$. For all $a,b,c \in \mathbb{Z}$, where $[x]$ denotes the congruence class of $x$ modulo $n$, show that $[a]\cdot ([b]+[c]) = [a]\cdot[b] + [a] \cdot [c]$ and $([b]+[c])\cdot [a] = [b]\cdot[a] + [c] \cdot [a]$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_708
nl_statement: Show that for any $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$ and any nonzero $X\in\mathbb{R}^2$, the angle between $X$ and $\rho_\theta(X)$ equals $\theta$ (hence $\rho_\theta$ is rotation by $\theta$).
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_692
nl_statement: Show that for every $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$, the rotation operator $\rho_\theta:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$, defined by $\rho_\theta(X)=R_\theta X$, fixes the origin.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_linear-gps_689
nl_statement: Show that $R_\theta=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix}$ belongs to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ for every $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abstract-gps_1108
nl_statement: Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\alpha=(1,2)$ and $\beta=(1,2,\dots,n)\in \mathrm{Sym}_n$. For any $1<i<n$, prove that $$(i,i+1)=\beta^{\,i-1}\,\alpha\,\beta^{-(i-1)}=\beta^{\,i-1}\,\alpha\,\beta^{\,n-i+1}.$$
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_abelian_420
nl_statement: Show that the generating function for the number $p(n)$ of partitions of $n$ is $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} p(n)\,x^{n} \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{1-x^{k}}.$
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: srdoty_alg_Z_n_824
nl_statement: Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer and let $a,b,c\in \mathbb{Z}$. Prove the following properties of congruence modulo $n$: $a \equiv a \pmod{n}$; if $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ then $b \equiv a \pmod{n}$; and if $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ and $b \equiv c \pmod{n}$ then $a \equiv c \pmod{n}$.
source: Doty, Lecture Notes on Abstract Algebra

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_758
nl_statement: Prove the \emph{polarization identity} $4 z\bar{w} = {\lvert z+w\rvert}^2-{\lvert z-w\rvert}^2 +i \bigl( {\lvert z+iw\rvert}^2 - {\lvert z-iw\rvert}^2 \bigr)$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_997
nl_statement: Prove that if the $2 \times 2$ matrix $M$ represents a complex number $a+ib$, then $M$ has two eigenvalues: $a \pm i b$ with the corresponding eigenvectors $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ \mp i \end{smallmatrix} \right]$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_1326
nl_statement:
Use $e^{z+w} = e^z e^w$ and $e^0 = 1 
ot= 0$ to show that $e^z 
ot=0$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$. In other words, show that if a function $f$ satisfies $f(z+w)=f(z)f(w)$ and $f(0) = 1$, then $f(z) 
ot= 0$ for all $z$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_2441
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open, $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic, and $f'(z) \not= 0$ for every $z \in U$. Show that $f$ is locally injective on $U$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_5157
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open, and $\psi \colon U \times [0,1] \to \mathbb{C}$ is a continuous function such that for each fixed $t \in [0,1]$, the function $z \mapsto \psi(z,t)$ is holomorphic. Then $h(z) = \int_0^1 \psi(z,t) \, dt$ is a holomorphic function on $U$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_5485
nl_statement: Suppose $f \colon \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{D}$ is holomorphic and $f(0) = 0$, then $\lvert f'(0)\rvert \leq 1$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_9443
nl_statement: If $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open and $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic and injective, then $f'(z) \not= 0$ for every $z \in U$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_18579
nl_statement: Let $z \in \mathbb{C}$. Prove that $\lvert e^z\rvert = e^{\Re z}$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_1146
nl_statement: Suppose a $2 \times 2$ real matrix $M$ is represented by $z \mapsto \xi z + \zeta \bar{z}$ . Show that $\det M = \lvert \xi\rvert^2 - \lvert \zeta\rvert^2$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_5555
nl_statement: Suppose $f \colon \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{D}$ is holomorphic and $f(0) = 0$, then $\lvert f(z)\rvert \leq \lvert z\rvert$ for all $z \in \mathbb{D}$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_15928
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open and $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic and injective. Show that $f'(z) \not= 0$ for every $z \in U$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_5367
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open, $p \in U$, and $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic, and $f'(p) \not= 0$. Then there is an open neighborhood $V$ of $p$ such that $f$ restricted to $V$ is injective.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_6276
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open, $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic, and $f'(p) \not= 0$ for some $p \in U$. Then there exists an open neighborhood $V$ of $p$ such that $f(V)$ is open and $f|_V$ is injective.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_6543
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open and $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic. If $p \in U$ and $f'(p) \not= 0$, then for sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, $f$ restricted to $\Delta_\delta(p)$ is injective.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_19034
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open, $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic, and $f'(p) \not= 0$ for some $p \in U$. Then there exist neighborhoods $V$ of $p$ and $W$ of $f(p)$ such that $f \colon V \to W$ is a bijection and $f^{-1}$ is holomorphic.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_20896
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ is open, $f \colon U \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic, and $f'(p) \not= 0$ for some $p \in U$. Then there exist open sets $V, W \subset \mathbb{C}$ with $p \in V \subset U$, $f(V) = W$, and $f|_V$ injective with holomorphic inverse.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_23494
nl_statement: Suppose $U \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is open, $f \colon U \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is continuously differentiable, $p \in U$, and $Df|_p$ is invertible (that is, $\det Df|_p \not=0$). Then there exist open sets $V, W \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $p \in V \subset U$, $f(V) = W$, the restriction $f|_V$ is injective (one-to-one), and hence a $g \colon W \to V$ exists such that $g(y) = (f|_V)^{-1}(y)$ for all $y \in W$. Furthermore, $g$ is continuously differentiable and $Dg|_y = {\bigl(Df|_x\bigr)}^{-1}, \qquad for all x \in V, y = f(x).$
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_1430
nl_statement: Suppose $L \in \mathbb{C}$. Show that $\lim_{z\to \infty} f(z) = L$ in the sense of the Riemann sphere if and only if for every $\epsilon > 0$ there exists an $M$ such that $\lvert f(z)-L\rvert < \epsilon$ whenever $\lvert z\rvert > M$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ca_ca_1436
nl_statement: Suppose $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$. Show that $\lim_{z\to z_0} f(z) = \infty$ in the sense of the Riemann sphere if and only if for every $M > 0$ there exists a $\delta > 0$ such that $\lvert f(z)\rvert > M$ whenever $\lvert z-z_0\rvert < \delta$.
source: Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2082
nl_statement: Let $m^*$ be the outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Suppose $A,B\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $m^*(B)=0$. Prove that $m^*(A\cup B)=m^*(A)$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2929
nl_statement: Prove that every bounded convex set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is Jordan measurable.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_4237
nl_statement: Show that the Cauchy product of two absolutely convergent series is absolutely convergent, and its sum equals the product of the sums.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_2192
nl_statement: Show that if $\{x_n\}$ is bounded and every convergent subsequence has the same limit $\ell$, then $x_n \to \ell$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-metric_1957
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a metric space such that every open cover of $X$ has a finite subcover. Prove that every sequence in $X$ has a convergent subsequence.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-funcs_497
nl_statement: Let $0 \leq c < 1$. Show that the series $\sum_{k=0}^\infty x^k$ converges uniformly on $[-c,c]$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-funcs_497
nl_statement: Show that the series $\sum_{k=0}^\infty x^k$ does not converge uniformly on $(-1,1)$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-approximate_335
nl_statement: Let $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x^2+1}$. Show that $f$ is analytic and find a power series for $f$ at $0$ and its radius of convergence.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-metric_1968
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a metric space such that every sequence in $X$ has a convergent subsequence. Prove that every open cover of $X$ has a finite subcover.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2077
nl_statement: Let $m^*$ be the outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined via coverings by countably many open rectangles. Prove that for any two subsets $A,B\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, we have $m^*(A\cup B)\le m^*(A)+m^*(B)$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2087
nl_statement: Let $m^*$ be the outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Suppose $R_1,\ldots,R_n$ are pairwise disjoint open rectangles. Prove that $m^*\Bigl(\bigcup_{k=1}^n R_k\Bigr)=\sum_{k=1}^n m^*(R_k).$
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_1938
nl_statement: Let $m^*$ denote the outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (defined via coverings by countably many open rectangles). Show that if $R\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is a closed rectangle, then $m^*(R)=V(R)$, where $V(R)$ is the volume of $R$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-several-vars-ders_2373
nl_statement: Let $(X,\lVert \cdot \rVert_X)$ be a normed vector space and $(Y,\lVert \cdot \rVert_Y)$ be a normed vector space. Show that if $A \in L(X,Y)$ is linear and bounded, then $A$ is continuous.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_2847
nl_statement: Show that if $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$ converges and $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \lvert a_n\rvert$ diverges, then the series is conditionally convergent.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_4256
nl_statement: Suppose $\sum a_n$ converges absolutely and $\sum b_n$ converges. Show that $c_n = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k b_{n-k}$ defines a convergent series with sum equal to the product of sums.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_2828
nl_statement: Suppose $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$ converges absolutely. Show that for any rearrangement of the series, the sum remains the same.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-several-vars-ders_1015
nl_statement: Let $\mathbb{R}[t]$ be the vector space of polynomials in one variable $t$. Let $D : \mathbb{R}[t] \to \mathbb{R}[t]$ be the derivative operator (derivative in $t$). Show that $D$ is a linear operator.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2489
nl_statement: Suppose $R \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is a closed rectangle and $f,g\colon R\to \mathbb{R}$ are Riemann integrable. Show that $\varphi(x)=\max\{f(x),g(x)\}$ and $\psi(x)=\min\{f(x),g(x)\}$ are Riemann integrable on $R$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_823
nl_statement: Suppose $R\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is a closed rectangle with one side of length $0$. For every bounded function $f\colon R\to \mathbb{R}$, show that $f$ is Riemann integrable on $R$ and $\int_R f = 0$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-several-vars-ders_2488
nl_statement: Let $A : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m$ be a linear operator. Prove that $A$ is differentiable at every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $DA(x)$ is equal to $A$ (as a linear map).
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-funcs_1442
nl_statement: Let $\{a_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$ be an enumeration of the rational numbers and define $g_n(x) \coloneqq \sum_{k=1}^{n} 2^{-k} f_n(x-a_k), \qquad f_n(x) \coloneqq \frac{x}{1+(n x)^2}.$ Show that $g_n \to 0$ uniformly on $\mathbb{R}$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2452
nl_statement: Suppose $R \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is a closed rectangle. Show that the set of Riemann integrable functions on $R$ is an algebra: if $f,g$ are Riemann integrable on $R$ and $a\in \mathbb{R}$, then $af$, $f+g$, and $fg$ are Riemann integrable on $R$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2466
nl_statement: Suppose $R \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is a closed rectangle and $f,g\colon R\to \mathbb{R}$ are Riemann integrable. Assume there exists a closed set $E\subset R$ with outer measure zero such that $f=g$ on $R\setminus E$. Show that $\int_R f = \int_R g$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_3775
nl_statement: Suppose $U\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is open and $S\subset U$ is a compact Jordan measurable set. Show that there exist finitely many closed rectangles $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ contained in $U$ such that $S\subset \bigcup_{j=1}^k P_j$ and the interiors are mutually disjoint; that is, $P_j^{\circ}\cap P_\ell^{\circ}=\emptyset$ whenever $j\ne \ell$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-real-nums_1211
nl_statement: Let $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$. Prove the reverse triangle inequality: $\bigl\lvert \lvert x\rvert - \lvert y\rvert \bigr\rvert \le \lvert x-y\rvert .$
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-funcs_1088
nl_statement: Let $\sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n (x-a)^n$ be a power series with radius of convergence $0<\rho\leq \infty$, let $I$ be as above, and let $f \colon I \to \mathbb{R}$ be its sum. Then $f$ is differentiable and $f'(x) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty (n+1)c_{n+1} (x-a)^n ,$ with radius of convergence equal to $\rho$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-approximate_1526
nl_statement: Suppose $f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k z^k$ is a convergent power series and $\{ z_n \}_{n=1}^\infty$ is a sequence of nonzero complex numbers converging to $0$, such that $f(z_n) = 0$ for all $n$. Show that $a_k = 0$ for every $k$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_4250
nl_statement: Suppose $\sum a_n$ and $\sum b_n$ are absolutely convergent series. Show that $\sum c_n$ defined by $c_n = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k b_{n-k}$ converges absolutely and $\sum c_n = (\sum a_n)(\sum b_n)$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_4420
nl_statement: Suppose $\sum_{n=1}^\infty x_n$ is a series with bounded partial sums, $\lambda_n \to 0$, and $\sum \lvert \lambda_{n+1} - \lambda_n \rvert$ converges. Show that $\sum \lambda_n x_n$ converges.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-funcs_1359
nl_statement: Define: a sequence $f_n \colon \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ \emph{converges uniformly on compact subsets} if for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the sequence $f_n$ converges uniformly on $[-k,k]$. Prove that if $f_n$ are continuous and converge uniformly on compact subsets, then the limit is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_3468
nl_statement: Let $U \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a connected open set and let $f \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ be harmonic (that is, twice continuously differentiable with $f_{xx}+f_{yy}=0$ on $U$). Prove the maximum principle: if $f$ attains a maximum at some $p \in U$, then $f$ is constant on $U$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-funcs_734
nl_statement: Let $f_n \colon [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be Riemann integrable and suppose $f_n \to f$ uniformly on $[a,b]$. Then $f$ is Riemann integrable and $\int_a^b f = \lim_{n\to\infty} \int_a^b f_n .$
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-several-vars-ders_999
nl_statement: Let $k : [0,1]^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous. Show that $L : C([0,1],\mathbb{R}) \to C([0,1],\mathbb{R})$ defined by $Lf(y) = \int_0^1 k(x,y)f(x) dx$ is a linear operator. That is, first show that $L$ is well-defined by showing that $Lf$ is continuous whenever $f$ is, and then showing that $L$ is linear.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-der_1129
nl_statement: Let $f \colon (a,b)\to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous and differentiable on $(a,b)\setminus\{c\}$ for some $c\in(a,b)$. Assume $\lim_{x\to c} f'(x)=L$ exists. Prove that $f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $f'(c)=L$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-metric_1348
nl_statement: Prove that in a metric space, $S$ is open if and only if for every $p \in S$ there is an $\epsilon > 0$ such that $B(p,\epsilon) \subset S$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_694
nl_statement: Let $\{ x_n \}_{n=1}^\infty$ be a convergent monotone sequence. Suppose there exists a $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\lim_{n\to \infty} x_n = x_k .$ Show that $x_n = x_k$ for all $n \geq k$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_1932
nl_statement: Suppose $X\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is such that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists a set $Y\supset X$ with $m^*(Y)\le \epsilon$, where $m^*$ is the outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Prove that $X$ has measure zero (that is, $m^*(X)=0$).
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-seq-ser_4414
nl_statement: Suppose $\sum_{n=1}^\infty x_n$ is a series whose sequence of partial sums is bounded, and $\{\lambda_n\}$ is a sequence with $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} \lambda_n = 0$ and $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \lvert \lambda_{n+1} - \lambda_n \rvert$ convergent. Show that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \lambda_n x_n$ converges.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2583
nl_statement: Let $R\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a closed rectangle and let $f\colon R\to \mathbb{R}$ be Riemann integrable with $f(x)\ge 0$ for all $x\in R$. Show that if $\int_R f=0$, then there exists a set $E\subset R$ of outer measure zero such that $f(x)=0$ for all $x\in R\setminus E$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_2067
nl_statement: Let $m^*$ be the outer measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by $m^*(S)=\inf\Big\{\sum_{j=1}^{\infty} V(R_j) : S\subset \bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty} R_j, R_j open rectangles\Big\}.$ Define instead $\mu^*(S)=\inf\Big\{\sum_{j\in I} V(R_j) : S\subset \bigcup_{j\in I} R_j, I finite or countably infinite, R_j open rectangles\Big\}.$ Prove that for every $S\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $\mu^*(S)=m^*(S)$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-riemann_572
nl_statement: Let $f \colon [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded function. Suppose there exists a sequence of partitions $\{ P_k \}_{k=1}^\infty$ of $[a,b]$ such that $\lim_{k \to \infty} \bigl( U(P_k,f) - L(P_k,f) \bigr) = 0 .$ Show that $f$ is Riemann integrable and that $\int_a^b f = \lim_{k \to \infty} U(P_k,f) = \lim_{k \to \infty} L(P_k,f) .$
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-riemann_626
nl_statement: Suppose $f \colon [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is Riemann integrable. Let $\epsilon > 0$ be given. Then show that there exists a partition $P = \{ x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_n \}$ such that for every set of numbers $\{ c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n \}$ with $c_k \in [x_{k-1},x_k]$ for all $k$, we have $\lvert \int_a^b f - \sum_{k=1}^n f(c_k) \Delta x_k \rvert < \epsilon .$ Here $\Delta x_k \coloneqq x_k - x_{k-1}$ for each $k$ whenever a partition $P = \{x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ is used.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-der_478
nl_statement: Suppose $f \colon I \to \mathbb{R}$ is differentiable at $c \in I$. Prove that there exist real numbers $a$ and $b$ such that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ with $\lvert a+b(x-c)-f(x)\rvert \le \epsilon \lvert x-c\rvert$ whenever $x\in I$ and $\lvert x-c\rvert<\delta$. Equivalently, prove that there exists a function $g \colon I \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\lim_{x\to c}g(x)=0$ and $\lvert a+b(x-c)-f(x)\rvert= \lvert x-c\rvert g(x)$ for all $x\in I$ near $c$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-riemann_1152
nl_statement: Let $f \colon [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded function, $\{ a_n \}_{n=1}^\infty$ and $\{b_n \}_{n=1}^\infty$ be sequences such that $a < a_n < b_n < b$ for all $n$, with $\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = a$ and $\lim_{n\to\infty} b_n = b$. Suppose $f$ is Riemann integrable on $[a_n,b_n]$ for all $n$. Then $f$ is Riemann integrable on $[a,b]$ and $\int_a^b f = \lim_{n \to \infty} \int_{a_n}^{b_n} f .$
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-several-vars-ders_2250
nl_statement: Prove that for square matrices $A$ and $B$, $\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B)$. Hint: First prove the result when $B$ is elementary, then when $B$ is a product of elementary matrices, and then for all $B$. Try to avoid the Laplace formula if at all possible; not only is it inelegant, but it will lead to wrong proofs unless you are very careful with how some operations reorder rows or columns.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-several-vars-ders_2159
nl_statement: Using the standard euclidean norm $\mathbb{R}^n$, show: Suppose $A \in L(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^n)$ is defined for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ by $Ax = xa$ for a vector $a \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Then the operator norm $\lVert A \rVert_{L(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^n)} = \lVert a \rVert_{\mathbb{R}^n}$. (That is, the operator norm of $A$ is the euclidean norm of $a$.)
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-multivar-int_878
nl_statement: Suppose $R',R''\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ are rectangles such that $R=R'\cup R''$ is a rectangle and $R'\cap R''$ is a rectangle with one side of length $0$ (so $V(R'\cap R'')=0$). Let $f\colon R\to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $f$ is Riemann integrable on $R'$ and on $R''$. Show that $f$ is Riemann integrable on $R$ and $\int_R f = \int_{R'} f + \int_{R''} f .$
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: jirilebl_ra_ch-several-vars-ders_2164
nl_statement: Using the standard euclidean norm $\mathbb{R}^n$, show: Suppose $B \in L(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R})$ is defined for $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ by $Bx = b \cdot x$ for a vector $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Then the operator norm $\lVert B \rVert_{L(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R})} = \lVert b \rVert_{\mathbb{R}^n}$.
source: Lebl, Basic Analysis

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_365
nl_statement: Show that every compact, locally simply connected topological space has finitely generated fundamental group.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_232
nl_statement: Prove that the one-point compactification of $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ is homeomorphic to the unit sphere $S^{n}$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_319
nl_statement: Every proper map $f \colon X \to Y$ to a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ is a closed map.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_319
nl_statement: Every proper map \(f\colon X\to Y\) to a locally compact Hausdorff space \(Y\) is closed.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_159
nl_statement: A continuous bijection \(f \colon X \to Y\) from a compact space \(X\) to a Hausdorff space \(Y\) is a homeomorphism.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_530
nl_statement: In any Hausdorff space, every compact set is closed.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_310
nl_statement: Prove that every continuous map \(f\colon X\to Y\) from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is proper.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_310
nl_statement: Prove that every continuous map $f \colon X \to Y$ from a compact space $X$ to a Hausdorff space $Y$ is proper.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_183
nl_statement: Prove that any connected finite graph has finitely generated fundamental group.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_1191
nl_statement: Prove that every contractible space is connected and has trivial homotopy groups.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_232
nl_statement: Prove that the one point compactification of \(\mathbb{R}^{n}\) is homeomorphic to the sphere \(S^{n}\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_474
nl_statement: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be compact topological spaces. Prove that every open cover of \(X \times Y\) has a finite subcover.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_436
nl_statement: Prove that a closed subset of a compact space is compact.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_359
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a path connected topological space that admits a countable basis of simply connected open sets. Show that $\pi_1(X)$ is countable.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_472
nl_statement: If \(X\) and \(Y\) are topological spaces, prove that \(X \times Y\) is compact if and only if \(X\) and \(Y\) are both compact.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_495
nl_statement: Topological spaces \(X\) and \(Y\) are both compact just when their product is compact.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_135
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a Hausdorff space and $Y$ any topological space. If continuous maps $f,g \colon X \to Y$ agree on a dense subset of $X$, prove that $f=g$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_770
nl_statement: Take a Hausdorff, path connected and locally simply connected space \(X\). Prove that the deck transformation group of the universal covering space is precisely \(\pi_1(X)\), acting by \([x][y]=[x*y]\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_452
nl_statement: If \(X\) and \(Y\) are path connected Hausdorff topological spaces and \(f \colon X \to Y\) is a covering map with \(y_0=f(x_0)\), then the map $\pi_1(Y,y_0)/f_* \pi_1(X,x_0) \mapsto X_{y_0}$ is bijective.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_586
nl_statement: Every path connected and locally simply connected topological space \(X\) has a universal covering space \(\tilde{X} \to X\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_214
nl_statement: Let $\varphi\colon P\to Q$ be a smooth map of manifolds with $\dim P<\dim Q$. Show that the image $\varphi(P)$ is nowhere dense in $Q$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_49
nl_statement: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $x\colon[0,1]\to M$ be a path. Prove that $x$ is homotopic relative to $\{0,1\}$ to a smooth path.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_123
nl_statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces, and let $f,g \colon X \to Y$ be continuous. Let $A=\{x \in X : f(x)=g(x)\}$. If $Y$ is Hausdorff, prove that $A$ is closed in $X$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_123
nl_statement: Take two continuous maps \(f, g \colon X \to Y\). Let \(A \subset X\) be the set of points at which \(f=g\). If \(Y\) is Hausdorff, then \(A\) is closed.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_116
nl_statement: Prove that every proper local diffeomorphism \(f \colon P \to Q\) between manifolds without boundary, with \(Q\) connected, is a covering map.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_424
nl_statement: The morphism of fundamental groups \(f_* \colon \pi_1(X) \to \pi_1(Y)\) induced by a covering map \(f \colon X \to Y\) on a Hausdorff space \(X\) is injective.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_701
nl_statement: Prove that the only topological spaces with \(\mathbb{R}\) as a covering space are \(\mathbb{R}\) and \(S^1\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_337
nl_statement: Let $Y$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Prove that any closed injection $f \colon X \to Y$ is a homeomorphism onto its image. In particular, any proper injection $f \colon X \to Y$ is a homeomorphism onto its image.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_154
nl_statement: Suppose \(A\) is a subset of a topological space \(X\). Prove that \(A \subseteq \overline{A}\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_307
nl_statement: Take a free group action on a metric space \(X\) by a group of isometries \(\Gamma\) with discrete orbits. Prove that the quotient map \(X \to X/\Gamma\) is a locally isometric covering map.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_227
nl_statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds and let $f\in C^0(M,N)$. Show that $f$ is homotopic to a smooth map $M\to N$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_212
nl_statement: Suppose that \(X\) is a metric space and that \(\Gamma\) acts on \(X\) by isometries. Prove that \(\Gamma\) acts on \(X\) as a covering action if and only if the action is free with discrete orbits.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_7
nl_statement: If $X$ and $Y$ are subsets of Euclidean spaces with the subspace topologies, prove that a map $f \colon X \to Y$ is continuous (preimages of open sets are open) if and only if $f$ is continuous in the usual $\varepsilon$--$\delta$ sense.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_156
nl_statement: Prove that the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ is homeomorphic to any open ball in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_97
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $x,y,z\colon[0,1]\to X$ be paths. Prove that $(x*y)*z$ is defined if and only if $x*(y*z)$ is defined.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_62
nl_statement: Prove that the number \(n\) of sheets (which might be \(\infty\)) above an evenly covered open set is constant along any path in \(Y\). In particular, if \(Y\) is path connected, this number \(n\) is constant, and we say that the covering map is \(n\) to \(1\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_478
nl_statement: Let \(f \colon X \to Y\) be a surjective map. Suppose there exists a compact subset \(K \subset X\) with \(f(K)=Y\). Equip \(Y\) with the quotient topology induced by \(f\). Prove that \(Y\) is compact.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_478
nl_statement: Suppose $f \colon X \to Y$ is a surjective map from a topological space $X$, and suppose there exists a compact subset $K \subseteq X$ with $f(K)=Y$. Prove that $Y$ is compact in the quotient topology.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_941
nl_statement: Every map of sets \(f \colon S \to G\) to a group extends uniquely to a morphism of groups \(f \colon \langle S\rangle \to G\) from the free group on the set \(S\), mapping each \(s \in S\) to \(f(s)\), extending linearly to all words on the alphabet \(S\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_100
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $x\colon[0,1]\to X$ be a path. Let $\bar x$ denote the reverse path $\bar x(t)=x(1-t)$. Prove that $x*\bar x$ is homotopic relative to $\{0,1\}$ to the constant loop at $x(0)$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_555
nl_statement: Suppose that \(Y\) is a Hausdorff topological space which admits a universal covering space. Prove that a covering map \((X,x_0) \to (Y,y_0)\) is universal if and only if every covering map \((Z,z_0) \to (Y,y_0)\) has a unique morphism \((X,x_0) \to (Z,z_0)\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_336
nl_statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces with basepoints $x_0\in X$ and $y_0\in Y$. Prove that $\pi_1(X\times Y,(x_0,y_0))\cong \pi_1(X,x_0)\times \pi_1(Y,y_0)$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_142
nl_statement: Suppose \(A \subset X\) is a subset of a topological space \(X\). Prove that \(A \subseteq \overline{A}\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_97
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $x,y,z\colon[0,1]\to X$ be paths whose concatenations are defined. Prove that $(x*y)*z$ is homotopic relative to $\{0,1\}$ to $x*(y*z)$, and that $(x*y)*z$ is defined if and only if $x*(y*z)$ is defined.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_731
nl_statement: If a group \(\Gamma\) has a covering action on a simply connected and locally simply connected Hausdorff topological space \(Y\), then the quotient map \(p \colon Y \to \Gamma \backslash Y \coloneqq X\) is a universal covering map, so there is a group isomorphism $\pi_1(X) \xrightarrow{\cong} \Gamma.$
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_101
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $f,g \colon X \to \mathbb{R}^{n}$ are continuous. Then $f+g \colon X \to \mathbb{R}^{n}$ is continuous.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_243
nl_statement: Let $F\colon[0,1]\times X\to Y$ be a homotopy and write $f_t(\,\cdot\,)=F(t,\,\cdot\,)$. Let $x_0,x_1\in X$ and set $y_0=f_0(x_0)$, $y_1=f_1(x_1)$. Let $x\colon[0,1]\to X$ be a path from $x_0$ to $x_1$, and define $y\colon[0,1]\to Y$ by $y(t)=F(t,x(t))$, a path from $y_0$ to $y_1$. Define isomorphisms $x_*\colon\pi_1(X,x_0)\to\pi_1(X,x_1)$ and $y_*\colon\pi_1(Y,y_0)\to\pi_1(Y,y_1)$ by $x_*([\gamma])=[\bar x * \gamma * x],\qquad y_*([\delta])=[\bar y * \delta * y].$ Prove that the induced homomorphisms on fundamental groups satisfy $y_* \circ (f_0)_* \;=\; (f_1)_* \circ x_*\colon \pi_1(X,x_0)\to \pi_1(Y,y_1).$
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_145
nl_statement: Suppose that \(k\) is a field containing \(\mathbb{R}\) and of finite dimension as a real vector space. Then \(k=\mathbb{R}\) or \(k=\mathbb{C}\), up to isomorphism. In particular, the splitting field of any real or complex polynomial in one variable has degree at most \(2\) over \(\mathbb{R}\), and every complex polynomial in one variable splits into a product of linear factors over \(\mathbb{C}\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_502
nl_statement: Suppose that \(Z \subset \mathbb{C}\) is a domain in the complex plane and that \(g \colon Z \to \mathbb{C}\) is a complex analytic function defined in \(Z\). A logarithm for \(g(z)\) is a complex analytic function \(G \colon Z \to \mathbb{C}\) so that \(g(z)=e^{G(z)}\). Prove that \(g(z)\) has a logarithm \(G(z)\) just when both of the following conditions are satisfied: (1) \(g(z) \ne 0\) for any \(z \in Z\) and (2) \(g\) takes every loop in \(Z\) to a null homotopic loop in \(\mathbb{C}-\{0\}\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_105
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $x\colon[0,1]\to X$ be a path from $x(0)=x_0$ to $x(1)=x_1$. For any loop $y$ based at $x_0$, consider the loop $\bar x*(y*x)$ based at $x_1$. Prove that the assignment $[y]\mapsto [\bar x*(y*x)]$ induces an isomorphism of groups $\pi_1(X,x_0)\to\pi_1(X,x_1)$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_1196
nl_statement: If \(f \colon X \to Y\) is a Serre fibration, then the obvious maps $\pi_n(F,x_0)\to\pi_n(X,x_0)\to\pi_n(Y,y_0)$ fit together into a long exact sequence $\cdots \to \pi_n(F,x_0) \to \pi_n(X,x_0) \to \pi_n(Y,y_0) \to \pi_{n-1}(F,x_0) \to \cdots.$
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_886
nl_statement: Suppose that \(X\) is a path connected and locally simply connected topological space, with a covering by path connected open sets \(\{X_a\}_{a \in A}\), so that every finite intersection \(X_{ab} \coloneqq X_a \cap X_b\) is also path connected. Let \(\pi\coloneqq\pi_1(X,x_0)\) and \(\pi_a\coloneqq\pi_1(X_a,x_0)\), and so on. Take a group \(\Gamma\) and group morphisms \(\pi_a \to \Gamma\) which agree on every \(\pi_{ab}\), for every \(a,b\). Then there is a unique group morphism \(\pi \to \Gamma\) extending the given morphisms \(\pi_a \to \Gamma\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_covering-spaces_1064
nl_statement: Take a path connected and locally simply connected topological space \(X\), and a cover by path connected open sets \(X_a \subset X\) with path connected intersections \(X_{ab} \coloneqq X_a \cap X_b\), all containing some point \(x_0 \in X\). Let \(\pi\coloneqq\pi_1(X,x_0)\), \(\pi_a\coloneqq\pi_1(X_a,x_0)\), and so on. Then \( \pi=*_{\pi_{ab}} \pi_a \) is the amalgamation of all \(\pi_a\) over all \(\pi_{ab}\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_183
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\overline{X}=X \cup \{\infty\}$. Declare a set $U \subseteq \overline{X}$ to be open if either $U$ is open in $X$, or $U=\{\infty\} \cup (X \setminus C)$ for some compact $C \subseteq X$. Prove that this defines a topology on $\overline{X}$ (the one-point compactification of $X$).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_502
nl_statement: Let $f(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ be a continuous function of vectors $v_1,\dots,v_n \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ that is invariant under simultaneous orthogonal transformations: $f(Uv_1,\dots,Uv_n)=f(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ for every orthogonal matrix $U \in O(n)$. Let $Y$ be the set of all positive semidefinite symmetric $n \times n$ matrices. Prove that there exists a continuous function $g \colon Y \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(v_1,\dots,v_n)=g(A)$ for every choice of $v_1,\dots,v_n$, where $A$ is the Gram matrix with entries $A_{ij}=\langle v_i, v_j \rangle$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_543
nl_statement: Let $X=\overline{B} \subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be the closed unit ball, $A=\partial X$ its boundary sphere, and $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ the unit sphere. Define $f \colon X \to Y$ by $f(x)=\big(\cos(\pi \|x\|),\, \sin(\pi \|x\|)\, \tfrac{x}{\|x\|}\big)$ for $x \neq 0$ and $f(0)=(1,0)$. Prove that $f$ is injective on the interior $X \setminus A$ and that $f$ maps every point of $A$ to the single point $(-1,0) \in Y$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_448
nl_statement: Let \(X\) be a topological space and let \(\sim\) be an equivalence relation on \(X\) with quotient map \(q \colon X \to X/\!\sim\). Show that any continuous map \(h \colon X/\!\sim \to Y\) induces a continuous map \(h\circ q \colon X \to Y\). Conversely, show that a continuous map \(f \colon X \to Y\) arises in this way (i.e., \(f=h\circ q\) for a unique continuous \(h\)) if and only if \(f\) is constant on equivalence classes: \(f(x_1)=f(x_2)\) whenever \(x_1\sim x_2\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_538
nl_statement: Let \(X=[0,1] \subset \mathbb{R}\) and let \(Y=\{(\cos(2\pi t),\sin(2\pi t)) : t\in[0,1]\} \subset \mathbb{R}^{2}\). Define \(f \colon X \to Y\) by \(f(t)=(\cos(2\pi t),\sin(2\pi t))\). Prove that the quotient space obtained by identifying \(0\) and \(1\) in \(X\), i.e. \(X/\{0,1\}\), is homeomorphic to \(Y\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_329
nl_statement: If \(A \subset X\) is a subset of a topological space \(X\), then the closed subsets of \(A\) in the subspace topology are exactly the sets \(A \cap C\) for any closed set \(C \subset X\). Moreover, the closure of a subset \(S \subset A\) inside \(A\) is the intersection of \(A\) with the closure of \(S\) in \(X\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_448
nl_statement: Let $q \colon X \to X/{\sim}$ be the quotient map for an equivalence relation ${\sim}$ on a topological space $X$. A map $h \colon X/{\sim} \to Y$ is continuous if and only if $h \circ q \colon X \to Y$ is continuous. Conversely, a continuous map $F \colon X \to Y$ descends to a continuous map $X/{\sim} \to Y$ if and only if $F(x_1)=F(x_2)$ whenever $x_1 \sim x_2$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_fundamental-groups_24
nl_statement: Let $X$ be a topological space covered by open sets $\{X_a\}_{a\in A}$ and let $x\colon[0,1]\to X$ be a path. Prove that there exist real numbers $0=t_0<t_1<\dots<t_n=1$ and indices $a_0,\dots,a_{n-1}$ such that for each $i$ we have $x([t_i,t_{i+1}])\subset X_{a_i}$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_continuity_22
nl_statement: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a map of topological spaces. Show that $f$ is continuous if and only if for every subset $A \subseteq Y$ one has $\overline{f^{-1}(A)} = f^{-1}\!\left(\overline{A}\right)$.
source: McKay, Notes on Topology

name: benmckay_top_topology_556
nl_statement: Let \(X\) be a topological space. Prove that \(\left(A \times B\right)^{\circ}=A^{\circ} \times B^{\circ}\) and that \(\overline{A} \times \overline{B} = \overline{A \times B}\).
source: McKay, Notes on Topology
